title.zh: 卷八十八 列傳第七十六: 隱逸
title.raw: 卷八十八 列傳第七十六: 隱逸 Volume 88 Biographies 76: Recluses

sentences.zh: 眭誇 馮亮 鄭修 崔廓 子賾 徐則 張文詡

translations.literal: Sui Kua, Feng Liang, Zheng Xiu, Cui Kuo, his son Zhen, Xu Ze, Zhang Wenshu
translations.idiomatic: Sui Kua, Feng Liang, Zheng Xiu, Cui Kuo, Cui Zhen, Xu Ze, and Zhang Wenshu

sentences.zh: 蓋兼濟獨善，顯晦之殊，其事不同，由來久矣。

translations.literal: For benefiting all and cultivating oneself alone, and for the difference between manifest and hidden—their affairs are not the same; this has been so from of old.
translations.idiomatic: The paths of aiding the world at large and of perfecting oneself in solitude, and the contrast between public service and withdrawal, have never been the same; the distinction is ancient.

sentences.zh: 昔夷、齊獲全于周武，華矞不容于太公，何哉？

translations.literal: In antiquity Boyi and Shuqi were preserved whole under King Wu of Zhou, yet Huayu found no place with the Grand Duke—why?
translations.idiomatic: In olden days Boyi and Shuqi came through unscathed under King Wu of Zhou, while Huayu found no welcome with the Grand Duke—why was that?

sentences.zh: 求其心者，許以激貪之用；

translations.literal: Those who sought their hearts granted them use for stirring the greedy;
translations.idiomatic: For those who probed their inner motives, they were allowed a role in awakening the grasping.

sentences.zh: 督其跡者，矯以教義之風。

translations.literal: Those who scrutinized their tracks rectified them with the wind of moral teaching.
translations.idiomatic: Those who examined their conduct shaped them with the breeze of righteous instruction.

sentences.zh: 而肥遁不歸，代有其人矣。

translations.literal: Yet those who made a full withdrawal and did not return—each age has had such men.
translations.idiomatic: Yet men who withdrew completely and never came back—every age has had them.

sentences.zh: 故《易》稱「遁世無悶」，「不事王侯」。

translations.literal: Thus the Book of Changes says, "Withdrawing from the world without vexation," and "not serving kings and marquises."
translations.idiomatic: Hence the Book of Changes speaks of "withdrawing from the world without discontent" and of "not serving kings and lords."

sentences.zh: 《詩》云「皎皎白駒，在彼空谷」。

translations.literal: The Book of Songs says, "Bright, bright is the white colt, in that empty valley."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Songs says, "Bright, bright is the white colt, there in the empty valley."

sentences.zh: 《禮》云「儒有上不臣天子，下不事諸侯」。

translations.literal: The Book of Rites says, "Among scholars there are those who above do not serve the Son of Heaven, and below do not attend on the feudal lords."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Rites says that some scholars "do not serve the Son of Heaven above, nor attend on feudal lords below."

sentences.zh: 《語》曰「舉逸民，天下之人歸心焉」。

translations.literal: The Analects says, "Raise up withdrawn subjects, and the people of the realm will turn their hearts to you."
translations.idiomatic: The Analects says, "Promote reclusive worthies, and the people of the realm will give you their hearts."

sentences.zh: 雖出處殊途，語默異用，各言其志，皆君子之道也。

translations.literal: Though their going forth and withdrawal follow different paths, and speech and silence serve different ends, each expresses his aim—yet all are the way of the gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Though whether they enter service or withdraw, speak out or keep silent, differs from man to man, each declares his own purpose; all alike belong to the way of the gentleman.

sentences.zh: 洪崖兆其始，箕山扇其風，七人作乎周年，四皓光乎漢日。

translations.literal: Hongya foretold the beginning; Jishan fanned the breeze; the Seven Men arose in the Zhou year; the Four Hoary Heads shone in Han days.
translations.idiomatic: Hongya marked the beginning, Jishan spread the example, the Seven Worthies appeared in Zhou times, and the Four White-Heads shone in the Han.

sentences.zh: 魏、晉以降，其流逾廣。

translations.literal: From Wei and Jin downward, the current grew ever broader.
translations.idiomatic: From the Wei and Jin dynasties onward, the stream of reclusion grew ever wider.

sentences.zh: 其大者則輕天下，細萬物；

translations.literal: Among the greater sort, some held the realm lightly and made small of the myriad things;
translations.idiomatic: The greater among them treated the realm lightly and regarded the myriad things as small;

sentences.zh: 其小者則安苦節，甘賤貧。

translations.literal: among the lesser, some rested content in harsh integrity and found sweetness in base poverty.
translations.idiomatic: the lesser were content with austere principle and took humble poverty as their portion.

sentences.zh: 或與世同塵，隨波瀾以俱逝；

translations.literal: Some shared the world's dust and drifted away with the waves;
translations.idiomatic: Some mingled with the world and were carried off with its currents;

sentences.zh: 或違時矯俗，望江湖而獨往。

translations.literal: some defied the age and corrected custom, gazing toward rivers and lakes as they went alone.
translations.idiomatic: others defied their times and set themselves apart, looking toward rivers and lakes as they went their own way.

sentences.zh: 狎玩魚鳥，左右琴書，拾遺粒而織落毛，飲石泉而庇松柏。

translations.literal: They played with fish and birds, kept lute and books at hand, gathered fallen grain and wove shed feathers, drank from stone springs and sheltered beneath pines and cypresses.
translations.idiomatic: They delighted in fish and birds, kept lute and books close at hand, gathered stray grain and wove shed feathers, drank from stony springs, and took shelter under pine and cypress.

sentences.zh: 放情宇宙之外，自足懷抱之中。

translations.literal: They released their feelings beyond the cosmos and found sufficiency within their own breasts.
translations.idiomatic: They let their hearts roam beyond the universe and found contentment within themselves.

sentences.zh: 然皆欣欣於獨善，鮮汲汲於兼濟。

translations.literal: Yet all rejoiced in cultivating themselves alone, and few were eager to benefit all together.
translations.idiomatic: Yet all rejoiced in perfecting themselves alone, and few were urgent to aid the world at large.

sentences.zh: 夷情得喪，忘懷累有。

translations.literal: They leveled gain and loss in feeling and forgot the burdens they bore.
translations.idiomatic: They treated gain and loss alike and put aside the weight of worldly cares.

sentences.zh: 比夫邁德弘道，匡俗庇人，可得而小，不可得而忽也。

translations.literal: Compared with advancing virtue and spreading the Way, correcting custom and sheltering people, they may be deemed small, yet cannot be deemed negligible.
translations.idiomatic: Beside those who advance virtue, spread the Way, reform custom, and shelter the people, recluses may seem small in scale, yet they cannot be dismissed.

sentences.zh: 而受命哲王，守文令主，莫不束帛交馳，蒲輪結轍，奔走岩穀，唯恐不逮者，何哉？

translations.literal: Yet sage kings who received the Mandate and cultured rulers who kept the tradition—none failed to send silken cords racing back and forth and rush-wheeled carts wheel to wheel, hurrying to cliff and valley for fear of not reaching them—why?
translations.idiomatic: Yet sage kings who received the Mandate and cultured rulers who upheld tradition all sent silken gifts in haste and rush-wheeled carriages in train, hurrying to cliffs and valleys lest they fail to win such men—why?

sentences.zh: 以其道雖未弘，志不可奪，縱無舟楫之功，終有堅貞之操，足以立懦夫之志，息貪競之風。

translations.literal: Because though their Way was not yet broad, their resolve could not be wrested away; even if they had no merit of boat and oar, they still had steadfast integrity enough to set the coward's will upright and still the wind of greedy rivalry.
translations.idiomatic: Because though their Way had not been widely realized, their resolve could not be broken; even without the achievement of steering the state, their steadfast integrity was enough to stiffen cowards' hearts and quiet the wind of greedy rivalry.

sentences.zh: 與苟得之徒，不可同年共日，所謂無用以為用，無為而無不為也。

translations.literal: They cannot be reckoned in the same year and day as those who grasp what they can; this is what is called using the useless as use, and acting without acting yet leaving nothing undone.
translations.idiomatic: They cannot be mentioned in the same breath as those who seize whatever they can; this is what is meant by "using the useless as use" and "through non-action, nothing is left undone."

sentences.zh: 自叔世澆浮，淳風殆盡，錐刀之末，競入成群。

translations.literal: From the late age onward, manners grew thin and shallow and pure custom was nearly spent; at the tip of an awl or knife-edge, rivals rushed in throngs.
translations.idiomatic: Since the late age, when manners grew thin and shallow and pure custom all but vanished, men scrambled in crowds over the smallest profit.

sentences.zh: 而能冥心物表，介然離俗，望古獨適，求友千齡，亦異人矣！

translations.literal: Yet those who could darken their hearts beyond things, stand apart from custom, look to antiquity alone for fit, and seek friends a thousand ages distant—such men too were extraordinary!
translations.idiomatic: Yet those who could fix their minds beyond the things of the world, stand wholly apart from custom, take antiquity alone as their measure, and seek companions a thousand years away—such men were extraordinary indeed!

sentences.zh: 何必御霞乘雲而追日月，窮極天地，始為超遠哉！

translations.literal: Why must one ride mist and mount clouds to chase sun and moon, exhaust heaven and earth, before being deemed transcendent and far?
translations.idiomatic: Why must one ride the clouds and chase the sun and moon, or exhaust heaven and earth, before being called truly remote from the world?

sentences.zh: 案《魏書》列眭誇、馮亮、李謐、鄭脩為《逸士傳》。

translations.literal: According to the Book of Wei, Sui Kua, Feng Liang, Li Mi, and Zheng Xiu were entered in the "Biographies of Retired Scholars."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Wei lists Sui Kua, Feng Liang, Li Mi, and Zheng Xiu in its "Biographies of Retired Scholars."

sentences.zh: 《隋書》列李士謙、崔廓、廓子賾、徐則、張文詡為《隱逸傳》。

translations.literal: The Book of Sui lists Li Shiqian, Cui Kuo, Kuo's son Zhen, Xu Ze, and Zhang Wenshu in the "Biographies of Recluses."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Sui lists Li Shiqian, Cui Kuo, Cui Zhen, Xu Ze, and Zhang Wenshu in its "Biographies of Recluses."

sentences.zh: 今以李謐、士謙附其家傳，其餘並編附篇，以備《隱逸傳》云。

translations.literal: Now Li Mi and Shiqian are attached to their family biographies; the rest are all compiled in this chapter to complete the "Biographies of Recluses."
translations.idiomatic: Here Li Mi and Shiqian are placed with their family biographies; the rest are gathered in this chapter to complete the "Biographies of Recluses."

sentences.zh: 眭誇，一名旭，趙郡高邑人也。

translations.literal: Sui Kua, also named Xu, was a man of Gaoyi in Zhao commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Sui Kua, also called Xu, was from Gaoyi in Zhao commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖邁，晉東海王越軍謀掾，後沒石勒，為徐州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Mai was a military planning aide to Jin's Prince of Donghai, Sima Yue; later he submitted to Shi Le and became Inspector of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Mai served as military planning aide to Jin's Prince of Donghai, Sima Yue; later he submitted to Shi Le and became inspector of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 父邃，字懷道，慕容寶中書令。

translations.literal: His father Sui, styled Huaidao, was Director of the Secretariat under Murong Bao.
translations.idiomatic: His father Sui, styled Huaidao, was director of the Secretariat under Murong Bao.

sentences.zh: 誇少有大度，不拘小節，耽好書傳，未曾以世務經心。

translations.literal: Kua from youth had great breadth of mind, did not bind himself to small points, was devoted to books and records, and never let worldly affairs cross his heart.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Kua had a generous spirit, cared little for petty rules, loved books and records, and never troubled his mind with worldly affairs.

sentences.zh: 好飲酒，浩然物表。

translations.literal: He loved wine and was vast and free beyond the things of the world.
translations.idiomatic: He loved wine and lived with an expansive ease beyond the dust of the world.

sentences.zh: 年三十，遭父喪，須鬢致白，每一悲哭，聞者為之流涕。

translations.literal: At thirty he suffered his father's death; his beard and temples turned white, and each time he wept in grief those who heard him shed tears.
translations.idiomatic: At thirty he lost his father; his beard and temples turned white, and whenever he wept in mourning those who heard him wept as well.

sentences.zh: 高尚不仕，寄情丘壑。

translations.literal: Lofty in character, he would not take office and entrusted his feelings to hills and ravines.
translations.idiomatic: Noble in spirit, he refused office and gave his heart to hills and valleys.

sentences.zh: 同郡李順願與之交，誇拒而不許。

translations.literal: Li Shun of the same commandery wished to befriend him; Kua refused and would not consent.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shun of the same commandery wished to befriend him, but Kua refused.

sentences.zh: 邦國少長莫不憚之。

translations.literal: Young and old throughout the district all stood in awe of him.
translations.idiomatic: Young and old throughout the district stood in awe of him.

sentences.zh: 少與崔浩為莫逆之交。

translations.literal: In youth he and Cui Hao were sworn friends beyond all breaking.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he and Cui Hao were the closest of friends.

sentences.zh: 浩為司徒，奏徵為中郎，辭疾不赴。

translations.literal: When Hao became Minister of Works, he memorialized to summon Kua as Gentleman of the Palace, but Kua pleaded illness and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: When Hao became minister of works, he memorialized to summon Kua as gentleman of the palace, but Kua pleaded illness and declined.

sentences.zh: 州郡逼遣，不得已，入京都，與浩相見。

translations.literal: The province and commandery pressed and sent him off; unable to refuse, he entered the capital and met Hao.
translations.idiomatic: Pressed by provincial and commandery authorities, he had no choice but to enter the capital and meet Hao.

sentences.zh: 經留數日，唯飲酒談敘平生，不及世利。

translations.literal: He stayed several days, drinking wine and recounting their lives together, never touching worldly profit.
translations.idiomatic: He stayed several days, drinking and talking over old times, never touching worldly gain.

sentences.zh: 浩每欲論屈之，竟不能發言，其見敬憚如此。

translations.literal: Hao each time wished to argue and bend him, yet in the end could not speak; such was the respect and awe he inspired.
translations.idiomatic: Hao often wished to argue him into submission, yet could never bring himself to speak; such was the respect and awe Kua inspired.

sentences.zh: 浩後遂投詔書於誇懷，亦不開口。

translations.literal: Later Hao cast the imperial edict into Kua's bosom; Kua still did not open his mouth.
translations.idiomatic: Later Hao thrust the imperial edict into Kua's bosom, but Kua still would not speak.

sentences.zh: 誇曰：「桃簡，卿已為司徒，何足以此勞國士也？

translations.literal: Kua said, "Taojian, you are already Minister of Works—how is it worth troubling a man of the realm with this?
translations.idiomatic: Kua said, "Taojian, you are already minister of works—why trouble a man of the realm with such a thing?

sentences.zh: 吾便將別。

translations.literal: I am about to take my leave."
translations.idiomatic: I am leaving now."

sentences.zh: 」桃簡，浩小名。

translations.literal: "Taojian" was Hao's childhood name.
translations.idiomatic: "Taojian" was Hao's childhood name.

sentences.zh: 浩慮誇即還，時乘一騾，更無兼騎，乃以誇騾內之廄中，冀相維縶。

translations.literal: Hao feared Kua would return at once; Kua was riding a single mule with no spare mount, so Hao put Kua's mule in the stable, hoping thereby to detain him.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Kua would leave at once—Kua had only a single mule and no spare mount—Hao stabled Kua's mule, hoping to keep him there.

sentences.zh: 誇遂托鄉人輸租者，謬為御車，乃得出關。

translations.literal: Kua then entrusted himself to a fellow townsman who was delivering rent grain, falsely posing as the driver, and thus got out through the pass.
translations.idiomatic: Kua then slipped out through the pass by posing as the driver for a fellow townsman delivering rent grain.

sentences.zh: 浩知而歎曰：「眭誇獨行士，本不應以小職辱之，又使其人杖策復路，吾當何辭以謝也！

translations.literal: When Hao learned of it he sighed and said, "Sui Kua is a man who walks alone; he should never have been insulted with a petty post, and to make such a man whip his way home on the road—what words can I find to apologize!"
translations.idiomatic: When Hao learned of it he sighed and said, "Sui Kua is a man who walks his own path; he should never have been slighted with a petty post, and to send such a man whipping his way home—what apology can I possibly offer!"

sentences.zh: 」時朝法甚峻，誇既私還，將有私歸之咎。

translations.literal: Court law at the time was very severe; since Kua had returned on his own, he was liable to punishment for unauthorized departure.
translations.idiomatic: Court law was very strict at the time, and because Kua had returned without permission he faced punishment for unauthorized departure.

sentences.zh: 浩仍相左右，始得無坐。

translations.literal: Hao still assisted him on both sides, and only then did he escape conviction.
translations.idiomatic: Hao continued to shield him on every side, and only then did Kua escape punishment.

sentences.zh: 經年，送誇本騾，兼遺以所乘馬，為書謝之。

translations.literal: After a year he sent back Kua's original mule and also gave him the horse he himself had ridden, with a letter of apology.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he returned Kua's mule and also sent the horse he had ridden, with a letter of apology.

sentences.zh: 誇更不受其騾馬，亦不復書。

translations.literal: Kua again would not accept the mule or horse and wrote no reply.
translations.idiomatic: Kua again refused the mule and horse and sent no reply.

sentences.zh: 及浩沒，為之素服，受鄉人弔唁，經一時乃止。

translations.literal: When Hao died, Kua wore white mourning for him and received condolences from fellow townspeople; only after a season did he stop.
translations.idiomatic: When Hao died, Kua wore unadorned mourning for him and accepted condolences from fellow townspeople; only after a season did he cease.

sentences.zh: 歎曰：「崔公既死，誰能更容眭誇！

translations.literal: He sighed and said, "Now that Lord Cui is dead, who can still tolerate Sui Kua!"
translations.idiomatic: He sighed and said, "Now that Lord Cui is dead, who will still tolerate Sui Kua!"

sentences.zh: 」婦父巨鹿魏攀，當時名達之士，未嘗備婿之禮，情同朋好。

translations.literal: His wife's father, Wei Pan of Julu, was a renowned man of the time; he never observed the full rites due a son-in-law, treating Kua as he would a friend.
translations.idiomatic: His father-in-law Wei Pan of Julu was a celebrated man of the day; he never kept the full rites owed a son-in-law, but treated Kua as a friend.

sentences.zh: 或人謂誇曰：「吾聞有大才者必居貴仕，子何獨在桑榆乎？

translations.literal: Someone said to Kua, "I have heard that men of great talent must hold noble office—why do you alone linger in the evening of life?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone said to Kua, "I have heard that men of great talent always take high office—why do you alone linger in life's twilight?"

sentences.zh: 」遂著《知命論》以釋之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he wrote the "Treatise on Knowing Fate" to explain himself.
translations.idiomatic: He then wrote the "Treatise on Knowing Fate" to explain his choice.

sentences.zh: 及卒，葬日赴會者如市。

translations.literal: When he died, on the day of burial those who came were thick as a market.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, mourners at his burial filled the streets like a market crowd.

sentences.zh: 無子。

translations.literal: He had no sons.
translations.idiomatic: He left no sons.

sentences.zh: 馮亮，字靈通，南陽人，梁平北將軍蔡道恭之甥也。

translations.literal: Feng Liang, styled Lingtong, was a man of Nanyang and nephew of Liang's General Who Pacifies the North, Cai Daogong.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Liang, styled Lingtong, was from Nanyang and nephew of Liang's general who pacified the north, Cai Daogong.

sentences.zh: 少博覽諸書，又篤好佛理。

translations.literal: In youth he read widely in all books and was also deeply devoted to Buddhist principle.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he read widely and was deeply devoted to Buddhist teaching.

sentences.zh: 隨道恭至義陽，會中山王英平義陽，獲焉。

translations.literal: He followed Daogong to Yiyang; when Prince of Zhongshan Ying pacified Yiyang, Liang was taken captive.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Daogong to Yiyang; when Prince of Zhongshan Ying captured the city, Liang was taken prisoner.

sentences.zh: 英素聞其名，以禮待接。

translations.literal: Ying had long heard his name and received him with courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Ying had long heard of him and treated him with courtesy.

sentences.zh: 亮性清靜，後隱居嵩山，感英之德，以時展覲。

translations.literal: Liang's nature was pure and still; later he withdrew to Mount Song, grateful for Ying's kindness, and from time to time paid his respects.
translations.idiomatic: Liang was by nature quiet and pure; later he withdrew to Mount Song, grateful for Ying's kindness, and visited him from time to time.

sentences.zh: 英亡，亮奔赴，盡其哀慟。

translations.literal: When Ying died, Liang hurried to the funeral and gave full vent to grief.
translations.idiomatic: When Ying died, Liang hurried to mourn him and grieved to the utmost.

sentences.zh: 宣武嘗召以為羽林監，領中書舍人，將令侍講《十地》諸經，固辭不許。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanwu once summoned him to be Supervisor of the Forest of Feathers and concurrently Attendant of the Secretariat, intending to have him lecture on the Ten Stages and other sutras at court; he firmly refused and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanwu once summoned him as supervisor of the forest of feathers and concurrent attendant of the Secretariat, intending to have him lecture on the Ten Stages and other sutras at court, but he firmly refused.

sentences.zh: 又欲使衣幘入見，苦求以幅巾就朝，遂不強逼。

translations.literal: The emperor also wished him to enter audience wearing the official cap; Liang earnestly begged to attend court in a plain headcloth, and in the end was not forced.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also wished him to appear in official cap and dress; Liang begged earnestly to attend court in a plain headcloth, and was not pressed further.

sentences.zh: 還山數年，與僧禮誦為業，蔬食飲水，有終焉之志。

translations.literal: Returning to the mountains for several years, he made ritual and recitation with monks his occupation, ate vegetables and drank water, and had the will to end his days there.
translations.idiomatic: Back in the mountains for several years, he devoted himself to ritual and scripture with the monks, lived on vegetables and water, and meant to end his days there.

sentences.zh: 會逆人王敞事發，連山中沙門法。

translations.literal: When the rebel Wang Chang's affair erupted, the Buddhist monks of the mountains were implicated as well.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebel Wang Chang's plot was exposed, the monks of the mountains were implicated as well.

sentences.zh: 而亮被執赴尚書省，十餘日，詔特免雪。

translations.literal: Liang was seized and sent to the Secretariat; after more than ten days an edict specially pardoned and cleared him.
translations.idiomatic: Liang was seized and sent to the Secretariat; after more than ten days an edict specially pardoned and cleared him.

sentences.zh: 亮不敢還山，遂寓居景明寺，敕給衣食及其從者數人。

translations.literal: Liang dared not return to the mountains and lodged at Jingming Monastery; an edict supplied food and clothing for him and several attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Liang dared not return to the mountains and lodged at Jingming Monastery, where an edict provided food and clothing for him and several attendants.

sentences.zh: 後思其舊居，復還山室。

translations.literal: Later, longing for his old dwelling, he returned once more to his mountain chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Later, longing for his old home, he returned to his mountain dwelling.

sentences.zh: 亮既雅愛山水，又兼工思，結架岩林，甚得棲遊之適。

translations.literal: Liang had long loved landscape elegantly and was also skilled in design; he built structures among cliff and forest and found great delight in dwelling and roaming there.
translations.idiomatic: Liang had long loved mountains and waters and was also skilled in design; he built among cliffs and forests and found there the perfect ease of dwelling and wandering.

sentences.zh: 頗以此聞，宣武給其工力，令與沙門統僧暹、河南尹甄深等同視嵩山形勝之處，遂造閒居佛寺。

translations.literal: This became widely known; Emperor Xuanwu supplied laborers and ordered him, together with the chief of monks Seng Xian and Intendant of Henan Zhen Shen and others, to survey the scenic places of Mount Song, whereupon they built the Hermitage Buddhist Monastery.
translations.idiomatic: Word of this spread; Emperor Xuanwu supplied workmen and had him, together with the chief of monks Seng Xian, intendant of Henan Zhen Shen, and others, survey Mount Song's finest sites, where they built the Hermitage Buddhist Monastery.

sentences.zh: 林泉既奇，營制又美，曲盡山居之妙。

translations.literal: The woods and springs were already marvelous, and the construction was beautiful as well, fully expressing the wonder of mountain dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: The woods and springs were marvelous, the construction exquisite, capturing to the full the charm of life in the mountains.

sentences.zh: 亮時出京師。

translations.literal: Liang would at times come out to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Liang sometimes came to the capital.

sentences.zh: 延昌二年冬，因遇篤疾，宣武敕以馬輿送令還山，居嵩高道場寺，數日卒。

translations.literal: In the winter of the second year of Yanchang he fell gravely ill; Emperor Xuanwu ordered him sent back to the mountains in a horse litter; he lodged at Songgao Daochang Monastery and died within several days.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the second year of Yanchang he fell gravely ill; Emperor Xuanwu ordered him carried back to the mountains in a horse litter; he stayed at Songgao Daochang Monastery and died within a few days.

sentences.zh: 詔贈帛二百匹，以供凶事。

translations.literal: An edict bestowed two hundred bolts of silk for the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted two hundred bolts of silk for the funeral.

sentences.zh: 遺誡兄子綜，殮以衣蒨，左手持板，右手執《孝經》一卷，置屍磐石上，去人數里外，積十餘日，乃焚於山，灰燼處，起佛塔經藏。

translations.literal: He left instructions to his brother's son Zong: enshroud him in reddish garments, place a tablet in the left hand and one volume of the Classic of Filial Piety in the right, set the corpse on a boulder several li from men, leave it more than ten days, then burn it on the mountain; where the ashes lay, raise a stupa and scripture repository.
translations.idiomatic: He left instructions to his nephew Zong: dress him in plain reddish garments, place a tablet in his left hand and one volume of the Classic of Filial Piety in his right, set the body on a boulder several li from any dwelling, leave it for more than ten days, then burn it on the mountain; where the ashes fell, raise a stupa and a scripture repository.

sentences.zh: 初、亮以盛冬喪，連日驟雪，窮山荒澗，鳥獸饑窘，僵屍山野，無所防護。

translations.literal: At first, because Liang died in deep winter and snow fell day after day in the remote mountains and desolate ravines, birds and beasts were starving; a stiff corpse lay in the wild hills with nothing to guard it.
translations.idiomatic: At first, because Liang died in deep winter and snow fell day after day in the remote mountains and desolate ravines, birds and beasts were starving; his stiff corpse lay in the wild hills with nothing to guard it.

sentences.zh: 時有壽春道人惠需，每旦往看其屍，拂去塵霰。

translations.literal: At the time the Shouyang Daoist Huixu came each dawn to look upon the corpse and brush away dust and snow.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Shouyang Daoist Huixu came each morning to look upon the body and brush away dust and snow.

sentences.zh: 禽蟲之跡，交橫左右，而初無侵毀。

translations.literal: The tracks of birds and insects crossed back and forth on either side, yet at first there was no harm or ruin.
translations.idiomatic: The tracks of birds and insects crossed to and fro on either side, yet the body was not harmed.

sentences.zh: 衣服如本，唯風蒨巾。

translations.literal: The garments were as before; only the reddish headcloth had been blown away.
translations.idiomatic: The garments were unchanged; only the reddish headcloth had been blown away.

sentences.zh: 又以亮識舊南方法師信大栗十枚，言期之將來十地果報，開亮手，以置把中。

translations.literal: Also, because Liang had known the southern monk Xin, Xin sent ten large chestnuts, saying he looked to Liang's future reward of the Ten Stages; he opened Liang's hand and placed them in his grasp.
translations.idiomatic: Because Liang had known the southern monk Xin, Xin sent ten large chestnuts, saying he looked to Liang's future reward of the Ten Stages; he opened Liang's hand and placed them in his grasp.

sentences.zh: 經宿，乃為蟲鳥盜食，皮殼在地，而亦不傷肌體。

translations.literal: After a night the chestnuts were stolen and eaten by insects and birds; the shells lay on the ground, yet the flesh of the body was not harmed.
translations.idiomatic: After a night the chestnuts were eaten by insects and birds; only the shells lay on the ground, yet the body itself was not harmed.

sentences.zh: 焚燎之日，有素霧蓊鬱，回繞其傍，自地屬天，彌朝不絕。

translations.literal: On the day of cremation a pale mist rose thick and lush, circling about the pyre from earth to heaven, lasting the whole morning without cease.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of cremation a pale mist rose thick and lush, circling the pyre from earth to heaven and lasting the whole morning without cease.

sentences.zh: 山中道俗營助者百餘人，莫不異焉。

translations.literal: More than a hundred clerics and laymen of the mountains who assisted in the rites all marveled at it.
translations.idiomatic: More than a hundred monks and laymen of the mountains who assisted in the rites all marveled at it.

sentences.zh: 鄭修，北海人也。

translations.literal: Zheng Xiu was a man of Beihai.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xiu was from Beihai.

sentences.zh: 少隱于岐南凡穀中，依岩結宇，不交世俗，雅好經史，專意玄門。

translations.literal: In youth he withdrew to Fangu in the south of Qi, built a dwelling against the cliffs, kept no company with the world, elegantly loved the classics and histories, and devoted himself wholly to the dark gate of learning.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he withdrew to Fangu south of Qi, built a dwelling against the cliffs, kept apart from the world, loved the classics and histories, and devoted himself to the study of the profound.

sentences.zh: 前後州將，每徵不至。

translations.literal: Provincial governors before and after each summoned him, but he never came.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial governors summoned him repeatedly, but he never came.

sentences.zh: 岐州刺史魏蘭根頻遣致命，修不得已，暫出見蘭根，尋還山舍。

translations.literal: Wei Langen, Inspector of Qi, repeatedly sent urgent summons; Xiu had no choice but to come out briefly to see Langen, then soon returned to his mountain dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Langen, inspector of Qi, sent urgent summons again and again; Xiu had no choice but to come out briefly to see him, then soon returned to his mountain dwelling.

sentences.zh: 蘭根申表薦修，明帝詔付雍州刺史蕭寶夤訪實以聞。

translations.literal: Langen submitted a memorial recommending Xiu; Emperor Ming ordered the Inspector of Yong, Xiao Baoyin, to investigate the facts and report.
translations.idiomatic: Langen submitted a memorial recommending Xiu; Emperor Ming ordered the inspector of Yong, Xiao Baoyin, to investigate and report.

sentences.zh: 會寶夤作逆，事不行。

translations.literal: Just then Baoyin rebelled, and the matter came to nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Baoyin rebelled, and the matter came to nothing.

sentences.zh: 崔廓，字士玄，博陵安平人也。

translations.literal: Cui Kuo, styled Shixuan, was a man of Anping in Boling.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Kuo, styled Shixuan, was from Anping in Boling commandery.

sentences.zh: 父子元，齊燕州司馬。

translations.literal: His father Ziyuan was Administrator of Yan province under Qi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ziyuan was administrator of Yan province under Qi.

sentences.zh: 廓少孤貧，母賤，由是不為邦族所齒。

translations.literal: Kuo from youth was orphaned and poor; his mother was of low status, and for this reason the clan did not rank him among them.
translations.idiomatic: Kuo was orphaned and poor from youth; his mother was of humble birth, and for this reason the clan would not acknowledge him.

sentences.zh: 初為裏佐，屢逢屈辱，於是感激，逃入山中。

translations.literal: At first he served as a village aide, repeatedly met with humiliation, and thereupon stirred with emotion and fled into the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: He first served as a village aide, suffered repeated humiliations, and in a surge of feeling fled into the mountains.

sentences.zh: 遂博覽書籍，多所通涉，山東學者皆宗之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he broadly read books, penetrating many fields, and scholars east of the mountains all took him as their master.
translations.idiomatic: He then read widely and mastered many subjects, and scholars throughout the eastern provinces looked to him as their leader.

sentences.zh: 既還鄉，不應辟命。

translations.literal: When he had returned to his home district, he did not respond to summons.
translations.idiomatic: After he returned home, he refused every official summons.

sentences.zh: 與趙郡李士謙為忘言友，時稱崔、李。

translations.literal: With Li Shiqian of Zhao commandery he was a friend who needed no words; at the time they were called Cui and Li.
translations.idiomatic: He and Li Shiqian of Zhao commandery were friends who needed no words between them; people of the day spoke of them as Cui and Li.

sentences.zh: 士謙死，廓哭之慟，為之作傳，輸之秘府。

translations.literal: When Shiqian died, Kuo wept for him in deepest grief, composed a biography for him, and submitted it to the secret archive.
translations.idiomatic: When Shiqian died, Kuo mourned him with deep grief, wrote his biography, and submitted it to the imperial secret archive.

sentences.zh: 士謙妻盧氏寡居，每家事，輒令人諮廓取定。

translations.literal: Shiqian's wife, the Lady Lu, lived in widowhood; whenever household affairs arose, she would send someone to consult Kuo for a decision.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqian's widow, Lady Lu, would send someone to consult Kuo whenever a household matter needed deciding.

sentences.zh: 廓嘗著論言刑名之理，其義甚精，文多不載。

translations.literal: Kuo once wrote a treatise on the principles of punishment and law; its meaning was very precise, but most of the text is not recorded here.
translations.idiomatic: Kuo once wrote a treatise on penal law whose argument was exceedingly fine; most of the text is not preserved here.

sentences.zh: 隋大業中，終於家。

translations.literal: In the Daye era of Sui, he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daye reign of Sui, he died at home.

sentences.zh: 子賾，字祖浚，七歲能屬文。

translations.literal: His son Zhen, courtesy name Zujun, at age seven could compose literary pieces.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhen, courtesy name Zujun, could compose literary pieces at the age of seven.

sentences.zh: 容貌短小，有口辯。

translations.literal: His appearance was short in stature, but he had eloquence in debate.
translations.idiomatic: He was short in stature, yet gifted in eloquent speech.

sentences.zh: 開皇初，秦孝王薦之，射策高第。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang, Prince Xia of Qin recommended him; in the archery-examination he placed in the top tier.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kaihuang era, Prince Xia of Qin recommended him, and he placed at the top of the archery-examination.

sentences.zh: 詔與諸儒定樂，授校書郎，轉協律郎。

translations.literal: An edict ordered him to fix ritual music together with the Confucian scholars; he was appointed collator, then transferred to director of harmonies.
translations.idiomatic: By imperial edict he joined the scholars in fixing ritual music; he was appointed collator, then promoted to director of harmonies.

sentences.zh: 太常卿蘇威雅重之。

translations.literal: Director of sacrifices Su Wei greatly esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: Su Wei, director of sacrifices, held him in high esteem.

sentences.zh: 母憂去職，性至孝，水漿不入口者五日。

translations.literal: He left office on his mother's passing; his nature was utmost filial—he took no food or drink for five days.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to mourn his mother; utterly filial by nature, he took neither food nor drink for five days.

sentences.zh: 後徵為河南、豫章二王侍讀，每更日來往二王之第。

translations.literal: Later he was summoned as tutor to the Princes of Henan and Yuzhang, each day changing shifts between the two princes' mansions.
translations.idiomatic: He was later summoned as tutor to the Princes of Henan and Yuzhang, traveling between their mansions on alternate days.

sentences.zh: 及河南為晉王，轉記室參軍，自此去豫章。

translations.literal: When Henan became Prince of Jin, he was transferred to recorder of the staff; from this point he left Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Henan became Prince of Jin, he was transferred to recorder on the staff and ceased attending Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 王重之不已，遺賾書曰：

translations.literal: The prince valued him without cease, and sent Zhen a letter saying:
translations.idiomatic: The prince continued to esteem him highly and sent Zhen a letter that read:

sentences.zh: 昔漢氏西京，梁王建國，平臺東苑，慕義如林，馬卿辭武騎之官，枚乘罷弘農之守。

translations.literal: In antiquity the Han dynasty had its Western Capital, and the Prince of Liang established his state—at the Terrace Garden and Eastern Park, those who admired righteousness thronged like a forest; Sima Xiangru resigned from the post of armed escort, and Mei Cheng gave up the governorship of Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity the Han had its Western Capital and the Prince of Liang founded his state; at the Terrace Garden and Eastern Park, men drawn to righteousness gathered like a forest—Sima Xiangru quit his post as armed escort, and Mei Cheng relinquished the governorship of Hongnong.

sentences.zh: 每覽史傳，嘗竊怪之：何乃脫略官榮，棲遲籓邸？

translations.literal: Whenever I read the historical records, I have secretly wondered: why did they cast off official glory and linger at a prince's residence?
translations.idiomatic: Whenever I read the histories, I have privately marveled: why did they shrug off official honor and tarry at a prince's residence?

sentences.zh: 以今望古，方知雅志。

translations.literal: Looking from the present back to antiquity, one then knows their lofty aims.
translations.idiomatic: Viewing the past from the present, one finally understands their exalted purpose.

sentences.zh: 彼二子者，豈徒然哉！

translations.literal: Those two men—were they idle after all?
translations.idiomatic: Those two men—were they truly without purpose?

sentences.zh: 足下博聞強記，鉤深致遠，視漢臣之三篋，似陟蒙山；

translations.literal: Your learning is broad and your memory strong, probing deep to reach far—compared with the Han minister's three chests of books, it is like climbing Mount Meng;
translations.idiomatic: You are broad in learning and strong in memory, plumbing depths to reach what is distant—set beside the Han minister's three chests of books, it is like ascending Mount Meng;

sentences.zh: 對梁相之五車，若吞雲夢。

translations.literal: Facing the Liang chancellor's five cartloads of books, it is as if swallowing the cloud-dream marshes.
translations.idiomatic: set before the Liang chancellor's five cartloads, it is as though one could swallow the marshes of Yun and Meng.

sentences.zh: 吾兄欽賢重士，敬愛忘疲，先築郭隗之宮，常置穆生之醴。

translations.literal: My elder brother reveres the worthy and esteems scholars, honoring them until he forgets fatigue—first he built Guo Kui's palace, and constantly set out Mu Sheng's wine.
translations.idiomatic: My elder brother reveres the worthy and esteems scholars, honoring them until he forgets weariness—he first built a palace for Guo Kui and constantly set out the wine reserved for Mu Sheng.

sentences.zh: 今者重開土宇，更誓山河。

translations.literal: Now we reopen our domain and renew our oath over rivers and mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Now we reopen our fief and renew our oath over rivers and mountains.

sentences.zh: 地方七百，牢籠曲阜；

translations.literal: A territory of seven hundred li, encompassing Qufu;
translations.idiomatic: A domain of seven hundred li, enclosing Qufu;

sentences.zh: 城兼七十，包舉臨淄。

translations.literal: Seventy cities together, embracing Linzi.
translations.idiomatic: and seventy cities together, embracing Linzi.

sentences.zh: 大啟南陽，方開東閤。

translations.literal: Widely he opens Nanyang, and newly opens the Eastern Lodge.
translations.idiomatic: He throws wide the gates of Nanyang and newly opens the Eastern Lodge.

sentences.zh: 想得奉飛蓋，曳長裾，藉玳筵，躡珠履，歌山桂之偃蹇，賦池竹之檀欒。

translations.literal: I imagine you might ride under flying canopies, trail long robes, rest on tortoise-shell mats, tread pearl-toed slippers, sing of the mountain cassia's bending grace, and compose on the pool bamboo's luxuriant beauty.
translations.idiomatic: I imagine you riding beneath flying canopies, trailing long robes, resting on tortoise-shell mats, treading pearl-toed slippers, singing of mountain cassia bending in the wind, and composing on the luxuriant bamboo by the pool.

sentences.zh: 其崇貴也如彼，其風流也如此，幸甚幸甚，何樂如之！

translations.literal: His exalted nobility is like that, his refined elegance like this—how exceedingly fortunate; what joy could compare!
translations.idiomatic: Such is his lofty dignity, such his refined grace—how exceedingly fortunate; what greater joy could there be!

sentences.zh: 高視上京，有懷德祖；

translations.literal: Gazing high upon the upper capital, I cherish the thought of Dezhi;
translations.idiomatic: Looking up toward the upper capital, I cherish the memory of Dezhi;

sentences.zh: 才謝天人，多慚子建。

translations.literal: My talent falls short of heaven's chosen man; I am much shamed before Zijian.
translations.idiomatic: my talent falls short of heaven's chosen; I am deeply ashamed before Zijian.

sentences.zh: 書不盡意，寧俟繁辭。

translations.literal: The letter does not exhaust my meaning; I shall await a fuller statement.
translations.idiomatic: Words on paper cannot exhaust my meaning; I shall wait to say more.

sentences.zh: 賾答曰：

translations.literal: Zhen replied:
translations.idiomatic: Zhen replied:

sentences.zh: 一昨伏奉教書，榮貺非恆，心靈自失。

translations.literal: Yesterday I humbly received your instructive letter—the honor bestowed is beyond the ordinary, and my spirit has lost itself.
translations.idiomatic: Only yesterday I humbly received your instructive letter; the grace shown me is beyond the ordinary, and my spirit has lost its footing.

sentences.zh: 若乃理高《象系》，管輅思而不解；

translations.literal: If the reasoning is lofty as the Appended Phrases of the Changes, Guan Lu could ponder yet not understand;
translations.idiomatic: Were the reasoning as lofty as the Appended Phrases of the Book of Changes, Guan Lu might ponder it and still not understand;

sentences.zh: 事富《山海》，郭璞注而未詳。

translations.literal: The matter as rich as the Classic of Mountains and Seas—Guo Pu annotated it yet left parts unclear.
translations.idiomatic: were the subject as rich as the Classic of Mountains and Seas, Guo Pu might annotate it and still leave it unclear.

sentences.zh: 至於五色相宣，八音繁會，鳳鳴不足喻，龍章莫之比。

translations.literal: As for the five colors sounding together and the eight tones gathering in harmony—phoenix calls are insufficient metaphor, and dragon patterns cannot compare.
translations.idiomatic: As for the five colors sounding in concert and the eight tones joining in harmony—phoenix song is too slight a likeness, and dragon pattern cannot match it.

sentences.zh: 吳劄之論《周頌》，詎盡揄揚；

translations.literal: Wu Zha's discussion of the Zhou Odes—how could it fully convey praise?
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zha's discourse on the Odes of Zhou—how could it exhaust all praise?

sentences.zh: 郢客之奏《陽春》，誰能赴節？

translations.literal: The man of Ying playing the Spring in Yang—who could match the beat?
translations.idiomatic: The man of Ying performing the Spring in Yang—who could keep the measure?

sentences.zh: 伏惟令王殿下，稟潤天潢，承輝日觀，雅道邁于東平，文藝高於北海。

translations.literal: Humbly considering Your Highness the Prince, you inherit the moisture of heaven's ford and bear the radiance of the sun-pinnacle; in refined Way you surpass the Duke of Dongping, and in literary craft you rise above the Prince of Beihai.
translations.idiomatic: Humbly considering Your Highness, you inherit the moisture of heaven's ford and bear the radiance of the sun-pinnacle; in refined learning you surpass the Duke of Dongping, and in literary craft you excel the Prince of Beihai.

sentences.zh: 漢則馬遷、蕭望，晉則裴楷、張華。

translations.literal: In Han there were Sima Qian and Xiao Wang; in Jin, Pei Kai and Zhang Hua.
translations.idiomatic: Under Han there were Sima Qian and Xiao Wang; under Jin, Pei Kai and Zhang Hua.

sentences.zh: 雞樹騰聲，鵷池播美，望我清塵，悠然路絕。

translations.literal: The cock tree resounds with fame, the egret pool spreads its beauty—you look down on my humble dust while the path stretches far and quiet.
translations.idiomatic: The cock tree rings with fame, the egret pool spreads its luster—you gaze down on my humble dust from a road already far and still.

sentences.zh: 祖浚燕南贅客，河朔惰游，本無意于希顏，豈有心于慕藺。

translations.literal: Zujun is a surplus guest south of Yan, a lazy wanderer north of the Yellow River; originally I had no mind to hope toward Yan Hui, nor any heart to admire Lin Xiangru.
translations.idiomatic: Zujun is a tag-along guest south of Yan, an idle wanderer north of the Yellow River; I never had it in mind to emulate Yan Hui, nor any wish to admire Lin Xiangru.

sentences.zh: 未嘗聚螢映雪，懸頭刺股。

translations.literal: Never did I gather fireflies to reflect on snow, or hang my head and pierce my thigh with an awl.
translations.idiomatic: I never gathered fireflies to read by snowlight, nor hung my hair from a beam and pierced my thigh with an awl.

sentences.zh: 讀《論》唯取一篇，披《莊》不過盈尺。

translations.literal: Reading the Analects I take only one chapter; spreading open the Zhuangzi does not exceed a foot's width.
translations.idiomatic: In reading the Analects I take but a single chapter; in opening the Zhuangzi I do not pass a foot's breadth.

sentences.zh: 況復桑榆漸暮，藜藿屢空，舉燭無成，穿楊盡棄。

translations.literal: Moreover the mulberry and elm grow twilight; thistle and bean broth are repeatedly empty; raising the lamp brings no achievement, and shooting the willow is wholly abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, mulberry and elm draw on toward evening, thistle and bean broth are again empty, the lamp is raised without success, and the willow shot is wholly abandoned.

sentences.zh: 但以燕求馬首，薛養雞鳴，謬齒鴻儀，虛班驥ＩＺ。

translations.literal: But only—seeking a horse's head in Yan, nurturing a cock's crow in Xue, wrongly placed among the great ranks, falsely ranked among steeds renowned for fleet hooves.
translations.idiomatic: Yet like one who sought a horse's head in Yan, or raised a cock to crow in Xue, I am wrongly counted among great ceremonies and falsely ranked among steeds renowned for fleet hooves.

sentences.zh: 挾太山而超海，比報德而非難；

translations.literal: Holding Mount Tai and leaping the sea—compared with repaying virtue it is not hard;
translations.idiomatic: To hold Mount Tai and leap the sea would not be hard beside repaying your kindness;

sentences.zh: 堙昆侖以為池，匹酬恩而反易。

translations.literal: Filling Kunlun to make a pool—matching repaying grace is conversely easy.
translations.idiomatic: to dam Kunlun and make a pool would be easy beside returning your favor.

sentences.zh: 忽屬周桐錫瑞，唐水承家，門有將相，樹宜桃李。

translations.literal: Suddenly it fell to the Zhou paulownia to receive auspiciousness and the Tang water to sustain the house—at the gate are generals and ministers, and the trees fit for peach and plum.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly the Zhou paulownia received its auspicious omen and the Tang waters sustained the house—at your gate stand generals and ministers, and your trees are fit for peach and plum.

sentences.zh: 真龍將下，誰好有名；

translations.literal: The true dragon is about to descend—who would crave a name?
translations.idiomatic: The true dragon is about to descend—who would still crave a name?

sentences.zh: 濫吹先逃，何須別聽。

translations.literal: The careless flute-player flees first—what need for a separate audience?
translations.idiomatic: The careless flute-player slips away first—what need for another hearing?

sentences.zh: 但慈旨抑揚，損上益下，江海所以稱王，丘陵為之不逮。

translations.literal: Yet your kindly intent moderates and uplifts, diminishing the high and benefiting the low—therefore rivers and seas are called kings, and hillocks cannot reach them.
translations.idiomatic: Yet your kindly intent restrains and uplifts, diminishing the high and benefiting the low—therefore rivers and seas are called kings, and hillocks cannot match them.

sentences.zh: 曹植儻豫聞高論，則不殞令名；

translations.literal: If Cao Zhi perchance heard your lofty discourse, he would not lose his fair name;
translations.idiomatic: If Cao Zhi should chance to hear your lofty discourse, he would not lose his fair name;

sentences.zh: 楊脩若竊在下風，亦詎虧淳德。

translations.literal: If Yang Xiu secretly stood in the lower wind, he likewise would not harm his pure virtue.
translations.idiomatic: if Yang Xiu stood secretly in the lower wind, he likewise would not impair his pure virtue.

sentences.zh: 無任荷戴之至，謹奉啟以聞。

translations.literal: I cannot bear the utmost debt of gratitude; I respectfully present this note to report.
translations.idiomatic: I am overwhelmed by gratitude beyond bearing and respectfully submit this note to inform you.

sentences.zh: 大業四年，從駕汾陽宮，次河陽鎮。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Daye, he followed the imperial progress to the Fenyang Palace, halting at Heyang garrison.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Daye he accompanied the emperor to the Fenyang Palace and halted at Heyang garrison.

sentences.zh: 藍田令王曇于藍田山得一玉人，長三四寸，著大領衣，冠幘。

translations.literal: Wang Yan, magistrate of Lantian, at Mount Lantian obtained a jade figure three or four inches tall, wearing a large-collared robe and a kerchief-cap.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan, magistrate of Lantian, obtained on Mount Lantian a jade figure three or four inches tall, dressed in a large-collared robe and wearing a kerchief-cap.

sentences.zh: 奏之。

translations.literal: He presented it in memorial.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized the court about it.

sentences.zh: 詔問群臣，莫有識者。

translations.literal: The emperor questioned the ministers; none could identify it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor questioned his ministers, but none could identify it.

sentences.zh: 賾答曰：「謹案：漢文帝已前，未有冠幘，即是文帝以來所制也。

translations.literal: Zhen answered: "According to my investigation: before Emperor Wen of Han, there was no kerchief-cap—therefore it must have been made since Emperor Wen."
translations.idiomatic: Zhen answered, "According to my investigation, before Emperor Wen of the Han there was no kerchief-cap—this must therefore have been made since Emperor Wen."

sentences.zh: 臣見魏大司農盧元明撰《嵩高山廟記》云：『有神人，以玉為形，像長數寸，或出或隱，出則令世延長。

translations.literal: "I have seen in the Record of the Songshan Shrine by Grand Steward Lu Yuanming of Wei, which says: 'There is a spirit being fashioned in jade, an image several inches long, who sometimes appears and sometimes hides; when he appears the age is prolonged.'"
translations.idiomatic: "I have seen in the Record of the Songshan Shrine by Grand Steward Lu Yuanming of Wei the statement: 'There is a spirit being fashioned in jade, an image several inches long, who sometimes appears and sometimes hides; when he appears, the age is prolonged.'"

sentences.zh: 』伏惟陛下，應天順人，定鼎嵩、雒，嶽神自見，臣敢稱慶。

translations.literal: "'Humbly considering Your Majesty, responding to Heaven and following the people, you have fixed the tripod at Song and Luo—the mountain god has revealed himself; I dare proclaim felicitation.'"
translations.idiomatic: "'Humbly considering that Your Majesty responds to Heaven and follows the people, having fixed the tripod at Song and Luo, the mountain god has revealed himself—I dare proclaim felicitation.'"

sentences.zh: 」因再拜，百官畢賀。

translations.literal: Thereupon he bowed twice; all officials congratulated in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he bowed twice, and all the officials congratulated in turn.

sentences.zh: 天子大悅，賜縑二百匹。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven was greatly pleased and bestowed two hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven was greatly pleased and bestowed two hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 從駕往太山，詔問賾曰：「何處有羊腸阪？

translations.literal: Following the progress to Mount Tai, the emperor asked Zhen: "Where is the Sheep's Gut Pass?"
translations.idiomatic: On the progress to Mount Tai, the emperor asked Zhen, "Where is the Sheep's Gut Pass?"

sentences.zh: 」賾答曰：「臣案《漢書·地理志》，上党壺關縣有羊腸阪。

translations.literal: Zhen answered: "According to the Geography Monograph in the Book of Han, in Huguan county of Shangdang there is a Sheep's Gut Pass."
translations.idiomatic: Zhen answered, "According to the Geography Monograph in the Book of Han, Huguan county in Shangdang has a Sheep's Gut Pass."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「不是。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "That is not it."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "That is not the one."

sentences.zh: 」又答曰：「臣案皇甫士安撰《地書》，云太原北九十里，有羊腸阪。

translations.literal: He answered again: "According to the Terrestrial Book by Huangfu Mi, ninety li north of Taiyuan there is a Sheep's Gut Pass."
translations.idiomatic: He answered again, "According to the Terrestrial Book by Huangfu Mi, ninety li north of Taiyuan there is a Sheep's Gut Pass."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「是也。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "That is the one."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "That is the one."

sentences.zh: 」因謂牛弘曰：「崔祖浚所謂問一知二。」

translations.literal: Thereupon he said to Niu Hong: "Cui Zujun is what is called 'ask one and know two.'"
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he said to Niu Hong, "Cui Zujun is what people call 'ask one and know two.'"

sentences.zh: 五年，受詔與諸儒撰《區宇圖志》二百五十卷，奏之。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, he received an edict to compile with the scholars the Illustrated Gazetteer of the Realm in two hundred fifty volumes, and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he received an edict to compile with the scholars the Illustrated Gazetteer of the Realm in two hundred fifty volumes and presented it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝不善之，更令虞世基、許善心演為六百卷。

translations.literal: The emperor was not pleased with it and further ordered Yu Shiji and Xu Shanxin to expand it to six hundred volumes.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was displeased with it and ordered Yu Shiji and Xu Shanxin to expand it into six hundred volumes.

sentences.zh: 以父憂去職，尋起令視事。

translations.literal: On his father's mourning he left office; soon he was reappointed and ordered to resume duties.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to mourn his father but was soon recalled and ordered to resume his post.

sentences.zh: 遼東之役，授鷹揚長史。

translations.literal: In the Liaodong campaign he was made eagle-bearer chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: During the Liaodong campaign he was appointed eagle-bearer chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 置遼東郡縣名，皆賾之議也。

translations.literal: The names of commanderies and districts established in Liaodong were all Zhen's proposals.
translations.idiomatic: The names of the commanderies and districts established in Liaodong were all proposed by Zhen.

sentences.zh: 奉詔作《東征記》。

translations.literal: He received an edict to compose the Record of the Eastern Campaign.
translations.idiomatic: By edict he composed the Record of the Eastern Campaign.

sentences.zh: 九年，除越王長史。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was appointed chief of staff to the Prince of Yue.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was appointed chief of staff to the Prince of Yue.

sentences.zh: 于時山東盜賊蜂起，帝令撫慰高陽、襄國，歸首者八百餘人。

translations.literal: At that time bandits in Shandong rose like bees; the emperor sent him to pacify Gaoyang and Xiangguo, and over eight hundred who surrendered their heads returned.
translations.idiomatic: At that time bandits in Shandong swarmed like bees; the emperor sent him to pacify Gaoyang and Xiangguo, and more than eight hundred who surrendered returned home.

sentences.zh: 十二年，從駕江都。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he followed the progress to Jiangdu.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he accompanied the imperial progress to Jiangdu.

sentences.zh: 宇文化及之弑帝也，引為著作郎，稱疾不起。

translations.literal: When Yuwen Huaji murdered the emperor, he appointed Zhen as composition director, but Zhen claimed illness and would not take the post.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuwen Huaji murdered the emperor, he appointed Zhen composition director, but Zhen pleaded illness and refused the post.

sentences.zh: 在路發疾，卒于彭城，年六十九。

translations.literal: On the road he fell ill and died at Pengcheng, age sixty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: On the journey he fell ill and died at Pengcheng at the age of sixty-nine.

sentences.zh: 賾與河南元善、河東柳䛒、太原王劭、吳興姚察、琅琊諸葛潁、信都劉焯、河間劉炫相善，每因休假，清談竟日。

translations.literal: Zhen was on good terms with Yuan Shan of Henan, Liu Bing of Hedong, Wang Shao of Taiyuan, Yao Cha of Wuxing, Zhuge Ying of Langye, Liu Zhuo of Xindu, and Liu Xuan of Hejian; on every holiday they would converse in pure talk until the day ended.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen was close to Yuan Shan of Henan, Liu Bing of Hedong, Wang Shao of Taiyuan, Yao Cha of Wuxing, Zhuge Ying of Langye, Liu Zhuo of Xindu, and Liu Xuan of Hejian; on every holiday they would hold pure conversation until the day ended.

sentences.zh: 所著詞、賦、碑、志十餘萬言，撰《洽聞志》七卷，《八代四科志》三十卷。

translations.literal: His writings—odes, rhapsodies, inscriptions, and records—amounted to more than a hundred thousand characters; he compiled the Record of Comprehensive Inquiry in seven scrolls and the Record of Four Categories Through Eight Dynasties in thirty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: His writings in verse, rhapsody, inscription, and record totaled more than a hundred thousand characters; he also compiled the Record of Comprehensive Inquiry in seven scrolls and the Record of Four Categories Through Eight Dynasties in thirty scrolls.

sentences.zh: 未及施行，江都傾覆，咸為煨燼。

translations.literal: Before they could be put into practice, Jiangdu was overthrown and all were reduced to ashes in the fire.
translations.idiomatic: Before they could be put into use, Jiangdu fell and everything was consumed to ashes in the flames.

sentences.zh: 徐則，東海郯人也。

translations.literal: Xu Ze was a man of Tan in Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Ze was from Tan in Donghai commandery.

sentences.zh: 幼沈靜，寡嗜欲，受業于周弘正，善三玄，精於論議，聲擅都邑。

translations.literal: From youth he was deep and quiet, with few desires; he studied under Zhou Hongzheng, excelled in the Three Mysteries, was skilled in disputation, and his fame dominated the capital.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was withdrawn and quiet, with few desires; he studied under Zhou Hongzheng, mastered the Three Mysteries, excelled in debate, and his reputation filled the capital.

sentences.zh: 則歎曰：「名者實之賓，吾其為賓乎！

translations.literal: Ze sighed and said: "Fame is the guest of reality—am I to be the guest?"
translations.idiomatic: Ze sighed and said, "Fame is the guest of reality—am I then to be the guest?"

sentences.zh: 」遂懷棲隱之操，杖策入縉雲山。

translations.literal: Thereupon he embraced the resolve of reclusion, staff in hand, and entered Mount Jinyun.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he embraced the resolve to withdraw, took up his staff, and entered Mount Jinyun.

sentences.zh: 後學者數百人苦請教授，則謝而遣之。

translations.literal: Later several hundred scholars painfully begged him to teach; Ze declined and sent them away.
translations.idiomatic: Later several hundred scholars earnestly begged him to instruct them, but Ze refused and sent them away.

sentences.zh: 不娶妻，常服巾褐。

translations.literal: He did not marry, and constantly wore a cloth cap and brown garb.
translations.idiomatic: He never married and always wore a cloth cap and brown robes.

sentences.zh: 陳太建中，應召來憩於至真觀。

translations.literal: In the Taojian era of Chen, he answered the summons and came to rest at the Zhizhen Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taojian era of Chen he answered a summons and stayed for a time at the Zhizhen Abbey.

sentences.zh: 期月，又辭入天台山。

translations.literal: After a month he again took leave and entered Mount Tiantai.
translations.idiomatic: After a month he again withdrew and entered Mount Tiantai.

sentences.zh: 因絕粒養性，所資唯松水而已，雖隆冬冱寒，不服綿絮。

translations.literal: Thereupon he cut off grain to nourish his nature; his sole sustenance was pine water alone—though midwinter was bitterly cold, he wore no cotton quilt.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he abstained from grain to nourish his nature, sustaining himself only on pine-infused water; even in the depth of winter's cold he wore no cotton quilt.

sentences.zh: 太傅徐陵為之刊山立頌。

translations.literal: The Grand Tutor Xu Ling carved a mountain stele and composed a eulogy for him.
translations.idiomatic: The grand tutor Xu Ling had a stele carved on the mountain and composed a eulogy for him.

sentences.zh: 初在縉雲山，太極真人徐君降之曰：「汝年出八十，當為王者師，然後得道也。

translations.literal: When first on Mount Jinyun, the Transcendent Lord Xu descended to him and said: "When you pass eighty, you will become the teacher of a king—only thereafter will you attain the Way."
translations.idiomatic: When he was first on Mount Jinyun, the Transcendent Lord Xu descended to him and said, "When you pass eighty you will become a king's teacher; only then will you attain the Way."

sentences.zh: 」晉王廣鎮揚州，聞其名，手書召之曰：「夫道得眾妙，法體自然，包涵二儀，混成萬物，人能弘道，道不虛行。

translations.literal: When Prince Jin held Yangzhou in broad garrison, hearing his name he personally wrote to summon him, saying: "The Way obtains the myriad subtleties; its law embodies nature itself; it embraces the Two Powers and blends to form the ten thousand things. If a man can enlarge the Way, the Way does not travel in vain."
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Jin held broad garrison at Yangzhou, hearing his fame he wrote in his own hand to summon him, saying, "The Way obtains the myriad subtleties; its law embodies nature; it embraces the Two Powers and blends to form the ten thousand things. When a man can enlarge the Way, the Way does not travel in vain."

sentences.zh: 先生履德養空，宗玄齊物，深曉義理，頗味法門。

translations.literal: "Sir, you tread virtue and nourish emptiness, revere mystery and equalize things; you deeply understand principles of meaning and have tasted the gates of the dharma."
translations.idiomatic: "Sir, you tread in virtue and nourish emptiness, revere mystery and equalize all things; you deeply understand the principles of meaning and have savored the gates of the dharma."

sentences.zh: 悅性沖玄，恬神虛白，餐松餌術，棲息煙霞。

translations.literal: "You delight in nature's pure mystery, tranquilly spirit void and white; you dine on pine and consume formulas, dwelling in mist and rosy clouds."
translations.idiomatic: "You delight in nature's pure mystery, keep your spirit tranquil, void, and white; you dine on pine and consume elixirs, dwelling among mist and rosy clouds."

sentences.zh: 望赤城而待風雲，遊玉堂而駕龍鳳。

translations.literal: "Gazing toward Redwall while awaiting wind and clouds, roaming the Jade Hall while driving dragon and phoenix."
translations.idiomatic: "You gaze toward Mount Chicheng awaiting wind and clouds, roam the Jade Hall borne by dragon and phoenix."

sentences.zh: 雖復藏名台嶽，猶且騰實江、淮。

translations.literal: "Though you again hide your name on terrace peaks, your substance still soars in Jiang and Huai."
translations.idiomatic: "Though you hide your name on lofty mountain terraces, your worth still shines forth across the Jiang and Huai."

sentences.zh: 藉甚嘉猷，有勞寤寐。

translations.literal: "Your excellent counsel is greatly praised; it has wearied my waking and sleeping."
translations.idiomatic: "Your fine counsel is widely celebrated; it has long occupied my thoughts waking and sleeping."

sentences.zh: 欽承素道，久積虛襟，側席幽人，夢想岩穴。

translations.literal: "I reverently inherit the pure Way and have long stored an empty breast; I sit with seat askance for the recluse and dream of mountain caves."
translations.idiomatic: "I reverently honor the pure Way and have long kept an open heart; I sit with seat turned aside awaiting a recluse and dream of life in mountain caves."

sentences.zh: 霜風已冷，海氣將寒，偃息茂林，道體休悆。

translations.literal: "Frost wind has already turned cold; sea air will soon be chill; rest in the lush forest—the body of the Way finds its ease."
translations.idiomatic: "The frost wind has turned cold and the sea air is growing chill; rest in the deep forest and let your body of the Way find its ease."

sentences.zh: 昔商山四皓，輕舉漢庭；

translations.literal: "Long ago the Four Hoary Heads of Mount Shang lightly rose to the Han court;"
translations.idiomatic: "Long ago the Four Hoary Heads of Mount Shang readily entered the Han court;"

sentences.zh: 淮南八公，來儀籓邸。

translations.literal: "the Eight Lords of Huainan came in ritual to a prince's residence."
translations.idiomatic: "the Eight Lords of Huainan came to serve at a prince's residence."

sentences.zh: 古今雖異，山谷不殊。

translations.literal: "Past and present differ, yet valleys and hills are not different."
translations.idiomatic: "Times may change, but mountains and valleys remain the same."

sentences.zh: 市朝之隱，前賢已說。

translations.literal: "Reclusion within the marketplace—former sages have already spoken of it."
translations.idiomatic: "Sages of old already spoke of hiding in plain sight within the city."

sentences.zh: 導凡述聖。

translations.literal: To guide the common and declare the sage.
translations.idiomatic: To guide the ordinary and expound the sacred.

sentences.zh: 非先生而誰？

translations.literal: If not you, Master, then who?
translations.idiomatic: If not you, Master, then who?

sentences.zh: 故遣使人，往彼延請，想無勞東帛，賁然來思，不待蒲輪，去彼空穀。

translations.literal: Therefore I send an envoy to go there and invite you; I think you need not trouble yourself with eastern silks—come splendidly in thought; wait not for the rush-wheeled carriage—leave that empty valley.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore I send an envoy to invite you; I trust you need not trouble yourself with formal gifts—come forth splendidly at once; do not wait for a carriage of rush wheels to draw you from your empty valley.

sentences.zh: 希能屈己，佇望披云。

translations.literal: I hope you can humble yourself; I stand awaiting the parting of clouds.
translations.idiomatic: I hope you will condescend to come; I stand waiting for the clouds to part.

sentences.zh: 」則謂門人曰：「吾今年八十一，王來召我，徐君之旨，信而不征。

translations.literal: " Ze told his disciples: "I am eighty-one this year; the Prince has come to summon me—the words of Lord Xu are trustworthy and now fulfilled without further sign.
translations.idiomatic: " Xu Ze told his disciples, "I am eighty-one this year, and the Prince has summoned me; Lord Xu's prophecy has proved true."

sentences.zh: 」於是遂詣揚州。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he went to Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: " With that he set out for Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 晉王將請受道法，則辭以時日不便。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Jin was about to request instruction in the Way and its methods, Ze declined on the grounds that the time was not suitable.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Jin was about to receive instruction in the Way, Ze declined, saying the time was not auspicious.

sentences.zh: 其後夕中，命待者取香火，如平常朝禮之儀，至於五更而死。

translations.literal: That night he ordered his attendants to fetch incense and fire, as in his usual rites of morning audience, and at the fifth watch he died.
translations.idiomatic: That evening he had his attendants bring incense and performed the rites he usually observed at dawn; at the fifth watch he died.

sentences.zh: 支體柔弱如生，停留數旬，顏色不變。

translations.literal: His limbs were soft as in life; he remained for several tens of days, and his complexion did not change.
translations.idiomatic: His body remained supple as in life; he lay for several weeks, and his complexion did not change.

sentences.zh: 晉王下書曰：「天台真隱東海徐先生，虛確居宗，沖玄成德，齊物處外，檢行安身。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jin issued a document: "The true recluse of Tiantai, Master Xu of Donghai—empty certainty as his standard, subtle mystery as his completed virtue, equalizing things while dwelling outside, restraining conduct to settle his person.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jin issued a proclamation: "The true recluse of Tiantai, Master Xu of Donghai, took emptiness and certainty as his foundation, subtle mystery as his completed virtue, treated all things as equal while dwelling apart from the world, and disciplined his conduct to preserve his person.

sentences.zh: 草褐蒲衣，餐松餌朮，棲隱靈岳，五十餘年。

translations.literal: In grass cloak and rush garment, dining on pine and feeding on atractylodes, dwelling hidden on spirit peaks—for more than fifty years.
translations.idiomatic: Clad in grass and rush, feeding on pine and living on atractylodes, he dwelt hidden on sacred mountains for more than fifty years.

sentences.zh: 卓矣仙才，飄然騰氣，千尋萬頃，莫測其涯。

translations.literal: Transcendent talent surpassing others, spirit soaring free—a thousand fathoms, ten thousand leagues, none can measure its bounds.
translations.idiomatic: His transcendent gifts were extraordinary, his spirit lofty and free; like depths of a thousand fathoms or breadth of ten thousand leagues, none could fathom his limits.

sentences.zh: 寡人欽承道風，久餐德素，頻遣使乎，遠此延屈，冀得虔受上法，式建良緣。

translations.literal: I have reverently inherited the wind of the Way and long fed on pure virtue; repeatedly I sent envoys to invite you from afar, hoping devoutly to receive the supreme Law and firmly establish a good bond.
translations.idiomatic: I have long reverenced the wind of the Way and nourished myself on your pure virtue; again and again I sent envoys to invite you from afar, hoping devoutly to receive the supreme teaching and establish a worthy bond.

sentences.zh: 至止甫爾，未淹旬日，厭塵羽化，反真靈府。

translations.literal: He had only just arrived, not ten days full, when he wearied of the dust, transformed in feather, and returned to the true numinous realm.
translations.idiomatic: He had only just arrived, less than ten days ago, when he cast off the dusty world, ascended in transformation, and returned to the true realm of spirit.

sentences.zh: 身體柔軟，顏色不變，經方所謂屍解地仙者哉。

translations.literal: His body soft and supple, his color unchanged—is this not what medical classics call corpse liberation into an earthly immortal?
translations.idiomatic: His body remained soft and his complexion unchanged—is this not what the medical classics call corpse liberation and earthly immortality?

sentences.zh: 誠復師禮未申，而心許有在，雖忘怛化，猶愴於懷。

translations.literal: Truly teacher's rites were not yet fulfilled, yet a promise of the heart remains; though I forget sorrow at his transformation, grief still lodges in my breast.
translations.idiomatic: Though the rites of discipleship were never completed, my heart had already pledged itself to him; though I should rejoice in his transformation, sorrow still fills my breast.

sentences.zh: 喪事所資，隨須供給。

translations.literal: Whatever the funeral requires, supply it as needed.
translations.idiomatic: Provide whatever his funeral requires.

sentences.zh: 霓裳羽蓋，既且騰雲；

translations.literal: Rainbow robes and feathered canopies—already he mounts the clouds;
translations.idiomatic: Rainbow robes and feathered canopies—he has already ascended on clouds;

sentences.zh: 空槨餘衣，詎藉墳壟？

translations.literal: an empty coffin and leftover garments—how could he rely on mound and tomb?
translations.idiomatic: an empty coffin and leftover garments—what need has he of mound and tomb?

sentences.zh: 但杖舄在爾，可同俗法。

translations.literal: Only his staff and shoes remain, to show conformity with common custom.
translations.idiomatic: Only his staff and shoes remain, to show conformity with ordinary custom.

sentences.zh: 宜遣使人，送還天台定葬。」

translations.literal: You should send envoys to return him to Tiantai for proper burial."
translations.idiomatic: Send envoys to return him to Mount Tiantai for proper burial."

sentences.zh: 是時，自江都至天台，在道多見則徒步，云得放還。

translations.literal: At that time from Jiangdu to Tiantai, on the road many saw Ze walking on foot, saying he had been released to return.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, from Jiangdu to Mount Tiantai, travelers on the road often saw Ze walking on foot, saying he had been released to return.

sentences.zh: 至其舊居，取經書道法，分遣弟子，仍令淨掃一房，曰：「若有客至，宜延之於此。

translations.literal: When he reached his old dwelling, he took scriptures and Daoist methods and distributed them among his disciples; he also had a room swept clean and said, "If guests come, you should receive them here.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached his old dwelling, he took his scriptures and Daoist texts and distributed them among his disciples; he had a room swept clean and said, "If guests come, receive them here.

sentences.zh: 」然後跨石梁而去，不知所之。

translations.literal: " Then he crossed a stone bridge and departed—none knew where he went.
translations.idiomatic: " Then he crossed a stone bridge and departed—to where, no one knew.

sentences.zh: 須臾屍柩至，知其靈化，時年八十二。

translations.literal: In a moment the coffin with his corpse arrived; they knew of his spiritual transformation. He was then eighty-two years old.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward the coffin with his body arrived, and they understood that he had undergone spiritual transformation. He was eighty-two years old at the time.

sentences.zh: 晉王聞而益異之，賵物千段，遣畫工圖其狀，令柳{巧言}為之贊。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jin heard and was all the more astonished; he sent a thousand lengths of goods as funeral gifts, had painters depict his likeness, and ordered Liu Bian to compose an encomium for it.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jin heard this and was all the more astonished; he sent a thousand lengths of goods as funeral gifts, had painters depict his likeness, and ordered Liu Bian to write an encomium for it.

sentences.zh: 時有建安宋玉泉、會稽孔道茂、丹陽王遠知等，亦行辟穀道，以松水自給，皆為煬帝所重。

translations.literal: At the time there were Song Yuquan of Jian'an, Kong Daomao of Kuaiji, Wang Yuanzhi of Danyang, and others who also practiced the grain-avoidance Way, sustaining themselves on pine water—all were valued by Emperor Yang.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Song Yuquan of Jian'an, Kong Daomao of Kuaiji, Wang Yuanzhi of Danyang, and others also practiced the Way of abstaining from grain and sustained themselves on pine water—all were esteemed by Emperor Yang.

sentences.zh: 張文詡

translations.literal: Zhang Wenshu
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wenshu

sentences.zh: 張文詡，河東人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Wenshu was a man of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wenshu was from Hedong.

sentences.zh: 父琚，開皇中，為洹水令，以清正聞。

translations.literal: His father Ju, in the Kaihuang era, served as Magistrate of Huanshui and was known for purity and uprightness.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ju served as Magistrate of Huanshui during the Kaihuang era and was known for purity and uprightness.

sentences.zh: 文詡博覽群書，特精《三禮》。

translations.literal: Wenshu read broadly among books and was especially expert in the Three Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Wenshu read widely among the classics and was especially expert in the Three Rites.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝方引天下名儒碩學之士，文詡時游太學，博士房暉遠等莫不推伏之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen was drawing in famous Ru scholars and eminent learned men from all the empire, Wenshu was then visiting the Imperial Academy, and Erudite Fang Xianyuan and others all deferred to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen was gathering renowned scholars and eminent learned men from across the empire, Wenshu was at the Imperial Academy, and the erudite Fang Xianyuan and others all deferred to him.

sentences.zh: 書侍御史皇甫誕，一時朝彥，恆執弟子之禮，以所乘馬就學邀屈。

translations.literal: Attending Secretary Huangfu Dan was a leading figure of the court in his day and always observed the rites of a disciple toward him, using the horse he rode to go to the academy and invite and detain him.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Dan, Attending Secretary in the Imperial Library, was a celebrated figure of the court and always observed the rites of a disciple toward him; he would take the horse he rode and go to the academy to invite Wenshu to accompany him.

sentences.zh: 文詡遂每牽馬步進，意在不因人自致也。

translations.literal: Wenshu then always led the horse and walked alongside, his intent being not to advance himself by relying on others.
translations.idiomatic: Wenshu would always lead the horse and walk alongside, his intent being not to advance himself by relying on others.

sentences.zh: 右僕射蘇威聞而召之，與語大悅，勸令從官，文詡固辭。

translations.literal: Right Vice Director Su Wei heard of him and summoned him; after conversing with him he was greatly pleased and urged him to take office, but Wenshu firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: Su Wei, Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, heard of him and summoned him; after speaking with him he was greatly pleased and urged him to take office, but Wenshu firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 仁壽末，學廢，文詡策杖而歸，灌園為業。

translations.literal: At the end of the Renshou era the academy was abolished; Wenshu leaned on his staff and returned home, making irrigation and gardening his occupation.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Renshou era the academy was abolished; Wenshu took up his staff and returned home, making irrigation and gardening his livelihood.

sentences.zh: 州郡頻舉，皆不應命。

translations.literal: The province and commandery repeatedly recommended him, but he never responded to summons.
translations.idiomatic: The province and commandery repeatedly recommended him, but he never answered their summons.

sentences.zh: 事母以孝聞。

translations.literal: He became known for filial service to his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He became known for his filial devotion to his mother.

sentences.zh: 每以德化人，鄉黨頗移風俗。

translations.literal: He always transformed people through virtue, and the village and district considerably shifted their customs.
translations.idiomatic: He always transformed others through virtue, and his village and district gradually changed their ways.

sentences.zh: 嘗有人夜中竊刈其麥者，見而避之。

translations.literal: Once someone stole and reaped his wheat at night; Wenshu saw him and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Once someone stole and reaped his wheat at night; Wenshu saw him and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 盜因感悟，棄麥而謝。

translations.literal: The thief, moved by this, abandoned the wheat and apologized.
translations.idiomatic: The thief, moved by this, abandoned the wheat and apologized.

sentences.zh: 文詡慰諭之，自誓不言，固令持去。

translations.literal: Wenshu comforted and instructed him, swore himself not to speak of it, and firmly had him take the wheat away.
translations.idiomatic: Wenshu comforted him, swore himself not to speak of it, and firmly had him take the wheat away.

sentences.zh: 經數年，盜者向鄉人說之，始為遠近所悉。

translations.literal: After several years the thief told fellow townspeople of it, and only then was it known far and near.
translations.idiomatic: After several years the thief told his fellow townspeople, and only then was the story known far and near.

sentences.zh: 鄰家築牆，心有不直，文詡因毀舊堵以應之。

translations.literal: A neighbor built a wall with a mind not quite straight; Wenshu therefore tore down his old wall to match it.
translations.idiomatic: A neighbor built a wall that was not quite straight; Wenshu therefore tore down his old wall to match it.

sentences.zh: 文詡常有腰疾，會醫者自言善禁，文詡令禁之，遂為刀所傷，至於頓伏床枕。

translations.literal: Wenshu once had a pain in his lower back; it happened that a physician claimed skill in spell-binding; Wenshu had him perform it and was wounded by a blade, to the point of collapsing on bed and pillow.
translations.idiomatic: Wenshu once suffered from pain in his lower back; a physician who claimed skill in spell-binding treated him and wounded him with a blade, so that he collapsed on his bed.

sentences.zh: 醫者叩頭請罪。

translations.literal: The physician kowtowed and begged forgiveness.
translations.idiomatic: The physician kowtowed and begged forgiveness.

sentences.zh: 文詡遽遣之，因為隱，謂妻子曰：「吾昨風眩，落坑所致。
