translations.literal: Wenshu immediately sent him away and covered the matter for him, telling his wife and children, "Yesterday I had a dizzy spell from wind and fell into a pit—that is what caused it.
translations.idiomatic: Wenshu immediately sent him away and covered the matter for him, telling his wife and children, "Yesterday I had a dizzy spell and fell into a pit—that is what caused it.

sentences.zh: 」其掩人短，皆此類也。

translations.literal: " His covering of others' faults was all of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: " His way of covering others' faults was all of this kind.

sentences.zh: 州縣以其貧素，將加賑恤，輒辭不受。

translations.literal: The province and county, because he was poor and plain, were about to add relief and support, but he always declined and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: The province and county, seeing that he was poor and plain, were about to offer relief and support, but he always declined and would not accept.

sentences.zh: 嘗閒居無事，從容歎曰：「老冉冉而將至，恐修名之不立！

translations.literal: Once at leisure with nothing to do, he calmly sighed and said, "Old age comes on gradually—I fear a cultivated name will not be established!
translations.idiomatic: Once at leisure with nothing to do, he sighed calmly and said, "Old age comes on gradually—I fear a cultivated name will not be established!

sentences.zh: 」以如意擊幾自樂，皆有處所，時人方之閔子騫、原憲焉。

translations.literal: " He would strike the armrest with his ruyi scepter for his own pleasure, each blow landing in its place; men of the time compared him to Min Ziqian and Yuan Xian.
translations.idiomatic: " He would strike the armrest with his ruyi scepter for his own pleasure, each blow landing in its place; men of the time compared him to Min Ziqian and Yuan Xian.

sentences.zh: 終於家，鄉人為立碑頌，號曰張先生。

translations.literal: He died at home; fellow townspeople erected a stele in praise of him and called him Master Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home; his fellow townspeople erected a stele in praise of him and called him Master Zhang.

sentences.zh: 論曰：古之所謂隱逸者，非伏其身而不見也，非閉其言而不出也，非藏其智而不發也。

translations.literal: Discussion: What the ancients called recluses was not hiding the body so it would not be seen, not closing the words so they would not come forth, not concealing wisdom so it would not be released.
translations.idiomatic: Discussion: What the ancients called recluses was not those who hid their bodies from sight, sealed their words within, or buried their wisdom unspoken.

sentences.zh: 蓋以恬淡為心，不皦不昧，安時處順，與物無私者也。

translations.literal: Rather, with tranquil indifference as their heart, neither bright nor dim, they rested in the times, accorded with circumstance, and were without selfishness toward things.
translations.idiomatic: They took tranquil detachment as their heart, neither dazzling nor obscure, settled peacefully in their age and circumstances, and harbored no selfish designs toward the world.

sentences.zh: 眭誇忘懷纓冕，畢志丘園，或隱不違親，貞不絕俗；

translations.literal: Sui Kua forgot official caps and robes and fulfilled his resolve in field and garden; some hid without violating kinship, were chaste without cutting off the vulgar;
translations.idiomatic: Sui Kua set aside caps and robes of office and fulfilled his resolve among fields and gardens; some lived in reclusion without forsaking kin, remained steadfast without severing ties to the world;

sentences.zh: 或不教而勸，虛往實歸，非有自然純德，其孰能至此？

translations.literal: some urged without teaching, went forth empty and returned full—without natural pure virtue, who could reach this?
translations.idiomatic: some taught without lecturing and drew others empty-handed yet sent them home enriched—without innate purity of virtue, who could attain such heights?

sentences.zh: 然文詡見傷無慍，徐則志在沈冥，不可親疏，莫能貴賤，皆可謂抱樸之士矣。

translations.literal: Yet Wenshu, though injured, was without anger; Ze's aim lay in deep obscurity—none could draw him near or push him away, none could make him noble or base—all may be called men who embrace simplicity.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when Wenshu was harmed he showed no resentment, and Ze's mind dwelt in profound obscurity—neither intimacy nor distance could touch him, neither rank high nor low could define him; all may be called men who embrace unadorned simplicity.

sentences.zh: 崔廓感於屈辱，遂以肥遁見稱；

translations.literal: Cui Kuo, stirred by humiliation, came to be praised for his ample withdrawal;
translations.idiomatic: Cui Kuo, moved by insult, won fame through his resolute withdrawal from the world;

sentences.zh: 祖浚文籍之美，足以克隆堂構。

translations.literal: Zu Jun's literary beauty was sufficient to continue and enlarge the ancestral hall-structure.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Jun's mastery of letters was sufficient to continue and magnify the family's inherited achievement.

sentences.zh: 父子雖動靜殊方，其于成名一也，美哉！

translations.literal: Father and son, though active and still in different directions, in achieving fame were one—how fine!
translations.idiomatic: Father and son, though one moved in the world and one dwelt apart, alike attained renown—admirable indeed!
